pr_title: Sending non-blocking audit events to a webhook is retried on any error
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup
/sig auth
/sig api-machinery

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The API server should retry sending audit events to configured webhook sinks regardless of the type of HTTP error code it might receive from the webhooks to reduce the risk of audit events loss. More details on the current implementation and motivation for the change in #82088.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #82088

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
The PR title captures only the effect of the PR as a fix for issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/82088. The effect of the proposed change is a bit broader and it is to make behavior on errors configurable, depending on the use case (since it appears that use cases may have different requirements, e.g. see auditing). It will result in retrying requests to audit webhooks on any error that might occur during the send process.
The current behavior on errors is preserved as default for all other use cases (authenticator and authorizer), however during review it was questioned whether it should be refactored too. This potential change was decided to be deferred for its own PR because it's not directly related to this PR and in order not delay until consensus around how to address the issue is built. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83377 for details.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:
n/a

issue_context.title: Retry sending audit events on any webhook response error code
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
The api server should retry sending audit events to configured webhook sinks regardless of the type of HTTP error code it might receive from the webhooks.

**Why is this needed**:
While some components may live with failed data transmissions, this is a particularly sensitive topic for the audit area. The API server audit mechanisms must ensure that no other reasonable option exists before dropping an audit event that may be the only trace of malicious behavior in the cluster. It seems that the current implementation may be improved further in this direction.

Currently, when the API server is configured for non-blocking sending of audit events to a webhook audit sink backend, it will retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff, should there be an error in communicating with the webhook, as implemented [here]( https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/webhook.go#L95-L120).   

However, not all errors will trigger a retry. Some are considered transient and yield retry. Others simply stop the retry cycle. For example, it retries on receiving HTTP code `500`, but not on receiving `502`. The list of error codes that will yield a retry is actually quite small - three HTTP errors and one network error. Any other error will not trigger a retry and the audit events will be lost. 

The code comments explain that the retry will consider only recoverable failures, which may make sense in other cases, but as far as sending audit events to an audit backend webhook is concerned, it is not sufficient policy. A more robust approach would be to consider any error and give the backend service a chance to recover instead of relying on the error codes semantics and the webhook implementations interpretation of it. That is more inline with having the transmission of audit events as top priority.

/sig auth
/sig api-machinery

review_comments: I realize this is pre-existing code. But it looks like we don't fully respect the header; we don't wait for however long Retry-After requests us to. Could we fix that now?

I agree it's kind of "almost there" solution. But do we want to risk waiting as long as an external webhook tells us to, or we want the api server to have full control on the wait time between retries? And equally, does it make sense to retry before the recommended time at all? It seems to me that both approaches have downsides.

I would move the discussion in a separate PR though as this one is not precisely for this.
Would you open up an issue for this?
Comment here on when it might make sense to retry on all errors (versus DefaultShouldRetry) ?
